topStories.headline: Video Surfaces of SFPD Officer Lunging at Scooter Rider Before Fatal Mission Street Crash
topStories.dek: Surveillance footage obtained by the Public Defender's Office contradicts the police department's initial account of the October 12 death of Edwin Adams.
topStories.body:
Newly released surveillance footage shows a plainclothes San Francisco police officer crouching and lunging toward Edwin Adams, 56, as he rode an electric scooter southwest on Mission Street near Eighth Street on October 12 — seconds before Adams crashed fatally into a metal pole. The video, obtained by the San Francisco Public Defender's Office and shared with multiple news outlets on November 12, is the first publicly available footage capturing the moments leading to Adams' death.

On the day of the crash, SFPD said a warrant suspect had fled on a scooter and 'collided with a street fixture and suffered injury.' The department made no mention of any officer making physical contact with Adams before the crash. The new footage appears to show otherwise: an unmarked police vehicle blocked the roadway ahead of Adams, and a plainclothes officer emerged and made contact with him. Adams then went down, his head striking a pole, and he later died at the hospital.

The Public Defender's Office filed a formal complaint with the Department of Police Accountability, alleging officers violated departmental pursuit and use-of-force protocols. The complaint also accuses the department of violating its own honesty policy. 'Any reasonable officer would know that crouching down to tackle a person traveling rapidly on a scooter without a helmet posed significant danger to the person, to the officer, and potentially to members of the public in the area,' the complaint reads, signed by public defenders Zac Dillon and Brian Cox.

Adams was riding after police attempted to serve a warrant related to his ankle monitor — issued as a condition of release in a drug case. SFPD had not issued further comment beyond its original brief statement as of press time.

topStories.headline: Board Votes Unanimously to Let Street Vendors Cook and Sell Food From Home
topStories.dek: San Francisco's Board of Supervisors approved a Microenterprise Home Kitchen Operations ordinance on November 10, a measure championed by Mission District vendors who could not afford commercial kitchen rents.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on Tuesday, November 10, to allow residents to prepare and sell food from their home kitchens, adopting a state framework that dozens of other California counties have already embraced. The vote, which took less than two minutes and prompted no floor debate, was a direct response to pressure from Mission District street vendors.

The ordinance implements California's Microenterprise Home Kitchen Operations (MEHKO) program, which a 2019 state law made available for local governments to opt into. District 9 Supervisor Jackie Fielder introduced the legislation in September after vendors protested an earlier city ordinance that required them to use certified commissary kitchens — which can cost roughly $1,000 a month in rent, an expense many said they could not absorb.

Under the new rules, the San Francisco Department of Public Health will establish a permit program, priced at an $828 annual fee, to inspect and certify home kitchens. Permitted operators can sell up to 90 meals per week and earn up to $100,000 in annual sales, and may sell from their home or from a pushcart, wagon, or pedal-driven cart. Renters will also need landlord approval. The department will require a food safety manager certificate and food-handling training.

Proponents say the change will strengthen the city's diverse food culture, particularly along the Mission's sidewalks and commercial corridors. San Francisco joins Alameda, Contra Costa, Santa Clara and Marin counties in running its own MEHKO program.

topStories.headline: Supervisors Advance Plan to Rename Cesar Chavez Street 'Las Campesinas'
topStories.dek: The Board of Supervisors' Land Use and Transportation Committee this week took up an ordinance to rename the 3.2-mile Mission corridor, following a community process that chose the name honoring women farmworkers.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Land Use and Transportation Committee considered a resolution this week to rename Cesar Chavez Street 'Las Campesinas Street' — Spanish for 'female farmworkers' — continuing a process that began after sexual-abuse allegations surfaced against the late labor leader Cesar Chavez earlier this year.

District 9 Supervisor Jackie Fielder, who represents the Mission, introduced the renaming ordinance. She was joined by Board President Rafael Mandelman and Supervisors Shamann Walton and Myrna Melgar as co-sponsors. The proposal emerged from a working group convened by Mayor Daniel Lurie's office, which presented two finalist names — 'Las Campesinas' and 'Sí Se Puede' — at a community meeting last month. Of 668 public comments submitted online, 'Las Campesinas' led by a significant margin.

The street runs approximately 3.2 miles through Diamond Heights, Noe Valley, the Mission and down to the waterfront. Not everyone in the neighborhood is enthusiastic: some Mission businesses and residents have raised concerns that a longer, Spanish-language street name could create headaches for delivery services and address changes. The full Board of Supervisors must still approve the ordinance before any signs are changed.

Fielding also introduced a provision to waive the standard municipal transportation code requirement that keeps a changed street's former name on signs for five years, meaning Cesar Chavez's name would not appear in parentheses below the new name.

events.title: Mission Branch Library Reopening at 3359 24th Street
events.description: The Mission Branch Library reopens at its permanent home on 24th Street after a temporary relocation to 1234 Valencia St. Residents can return books or visit the restored branch starting this Saturday.

events.title: BART Bus Bridge: 24th Street Mission to Daly City
events.description: BART is suspending train service between 24th Street Mission and Daly City stations both days while crews install equipment for a new Communications-Based Train Control system. Free replacement buses — SamTrans express and Muni hoppers stopping at Glen Park and Balboa Park — will cover the gap; plan for up to 30 minutes of additional travel time.

events.title: Alemany Farm Volunteer Day
events.description: Join fellow neighbors for a regular volunteer workday at Alemany Farm, a community urban farm near the Alemany Farmers' Market. No experience necessary; all are welcome.

events.description: Neighbors gather to tend the beloved hillside garden stairway on Esmeralda Avenue. A regular community maintenance event open to all Bernal Heights residents.

events.title: Tasha Colby: Artist Talk & Pop-Up at RedBrick Ceramic Studio
events.description: Ceramic artist Tasha Colby hosts a free artist talk and pop-up sale at RedBrick Ceramic Studio in the Mission. Admission is free.

events.title: Ogden Tree Lighting – 4th Annual
events.description: Bernal Heights neighbors gather for the fourth annual Ogden Avenue tree lighting ceremony to kick off the holiday season and celebrate neighborhood beautification efforts on the hill.

events.title: Bernal Heights Library Winter Open House
events.location: Bernal Heights Branch Library, 500 Cortland Ave.
events.description: The Bernal Heights Branch Library hosts its annual winter open house, featuring live jazz, face-painting, and local crafts. Free and open to the community.

moreNews.headline: Bernal Heights Early-Education School Set to Close at End of School Year
moreNews.body: San Francisco Unified School District notified families at Junipero Serra Annex Early Education School in Bernal Heights in early November that the preschool program will not continue after the current school year ends. SFUSD officials described the change as a 'transition,' but parents receiving the letters said the message amounted to a closure notice. The letters went out just a month into the fall semester, leaving families scrambling for alternatives. The November 10 Mission Local report tagged the story under the Board of Education and noted the broader context of enrollment pressures on SFUSD.

moreNews.headline: Radio Habana to Add Daytime Café Service; Drawing Room Eyes January Return to Mission Street
moreNews.body: Two Mission District venue news items landed this week. Radio Habana, the long-running Cuban restaurant and live-music spot, announced a soft opening of a daytime café later this month, expanding its hours beyond evenings. Separately, The Drawing Room — which operated on 23rd Street from 2018 to 2021 before moving to 2675 Mission St. — is coming to 2401 Mission St. at the corner of 20th Street, with signage on the building reading 'coming January 2027.' Both items were reported in Mission Local's Mission Buzz column on November 11, 2026.
